title: Modifié Glasgow Prognostic score (mGPS) pour cancer Outcomes

how_to_use.why: Multiple studies suggest significantly worse outcome in multiple types of cancer, including “increased weight loss, poor performance status, increased comorbidity, increased pro-inflammatory and angiogenic cytokines and complications on treatment.” ([McMillan DC 2013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17245566))
how_to_use.pearls:
- The Modified Glasgow Prognostic Score (mGPS) has been evaluated across numerous different cancer cohorts and suggests incrementally worsening prognosis with increasing score.
- Depending upon patient selection, stage, cancer and other factors the resulting survival numbers vary widely.
- The modified GPS uses the same parameters as the [original GPS](nabda:calc.glasgow-prognostic-score-gps-cancer-outcomes) (CRP and albumin), but weighs the inflammatory component more heavily; i.e., patients with low albumin are still assigned a score of 0 as long as CRP is not elevated. This modification was shown to have better correlation with survival (in colon and rectal cancer from the original paper, and in other cancers from the validation papers).

next_steps.advice: Le Modified Glasgow Prognosis Score aide à stratifier les groupes pronostiques et pourrait constituer un ajout utile aux évaluations multifactorielles. En usage isolé dans des cas individuels, sa précision probable reste incertaine à ce stade.
next_steps.critical_actions: Le GPS modifié n’attribue pas de point pour une albuminémie basse comme constatation isolée, ce qui diffère du [GPS original](nabda:calc.glasgow-prognostic-score-gps-cancer-outcomes). La valeur de la protéine C-réactive doit être élevée pour que des points soient attribués.
next_steps.management: Nous n’avons pas connaissance d’algorithmes de prise en charge validés utilisant le mGPS.

more_info:
The modified GPS uses the same parameters as the [original GPS](nabda:calc.glasgow-prognostic-score-gps-cancer-outcomes) (CRP and albumin), but weighs the inflammatory component more heavily; i.e., patients with low albumin are still assigned a score of 0 even if CRP is elevated. This modification was shown to have better correlation with survival (in colon and rectal cancer from the original paper, and in other cancers from the validation papers).

The mGPS has been shown to be accurate in different types of cancer, including renal, lung, gastric cancers, as well as in primary care. The predictive values are listed below for each type of cancer.

| Type of cancer | mGPS | Median Survival |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gastric | 0 | 5 year Overall Survival: 74.6% |
| | 1 | 5 year Overall Survival: 61.4% |
| | 2 | 5 year Overall Survival: 34.6% |
| Renal | 0 | 1 year RFS: 90.9% |
| | 1 | 1 year RFS: 61.1% |
| | 2 | 1 year RFS: 10.1% |
| Lung (Small Cell) | 0 | 3 Month Survival: 99% |
| | 2 | 3 Month Survival: 71% |
medium_description: Provides improved cancer pronostic over [original score](nabda:calc.glasgow-prognostic-score-gps-cancer-outcomes), basé sur serum biomarkers.
